JPM.rationale: JPMorgan Chase demonstrates strong fundamental health with accelerating earnings trajectory: Q1 2026 revenue of $49.84B (+10% YoY) and EPS of $5.94 (+17.2% YoY) represent the strongest quarterly results in the available history. The bank maintains robust profitability with 31.5% net margin and 16.2% ROE, while operating margin of 39.9% reflects strong operational efficiency. Balance sheet is fortress-like with $364B equity supporting $4.9T in assets. The bank just passed all Fed stress tests and announced a 10% dividend hike plus $50B buyback authorization, providing clear capital return visibility. Valuation is reasonable at 15.5x P/E (mid-range of 13.7-17.8x over the past year) and 2.5x P/B, not expensive given the earnings momentum. Near-term catalyst exists with Q2 2026 earnings on July 14 where consensus expects $5.44 EPS (+9.7% YoY), and the bank has beaten estimates for four consecutive quarters. European expansion into France, Italy, and Spain announced June 16 provides a medium-term growth vector. Key risks include CEO Dimon's May 27 warning of expenses potentially reaching $106B (up from $105B guidance), DOJ subpoenas over debanking practices, and the hawkish Fed shift potentially pressuring NII growth. However, the bank's 7% NII growth target becomes more achievable with higher rates, and the diversified business model across consumer banking, CIB, and AWM provides resilience.
